target: Decide the existence of a symmetric weighing matrix SW(25,16): a 25x25 matrix W over {-1,0,1} with W = W^T and W W^T = 16 I. Same-lane alternates, in order, if SW(25,16) is decided or blocked: SW(27,16), SW(29,16).

open_attestation.quote: leaving n in {25,27,29} as the remaining open instances for w=16

pre_freeze_priority_screen.result: status (b): listed open; no later resolution found in the read scope (includes Goldberger-Ben-Av-Dula-Strassler arXiv:2603.17552 / Discrete Math. 350 (2026) 115367, which solves SW(23,16), SW(28,25), SW(30,17) but not n = 25, 27, 29; Dinitz and Munemasa pages post only non-symmetric W(25|27|29,16)). Blocked: Rosin NeurIPS-25 workshop version, published DM version, Georgiou 2023, Ben-Av 2024, Handbook Table 2.88. A miss is not novelty.

success_gate: (a) An explicit SW(25,16) (or an alternate) that passes a parent definition-first checker with intended-reason negative controls, an independent Codex CLI gpt-6.1-sol verifier and a Claude CLI claude-opus-5-5 prompt-only checker, plus a re-run of the producer; or (b) a complete nonexistence proof with certificates (DRAT verified by the parent drat-trim, every reduction written and reviewed by both CLI model families). Then a post-result priority re-check against primary sources before any claim; never "first".
known_constraints: circulant and back-circulant models are excluded (odd-order CW(n,16) requires n to be an odd multiple of 21 or 31)
zero diagonal is impossible (trace = 4(p-q) with p+q = 25 odd)
primitive automorphism groups of rank <= 5 are excluded by the Egan-O Cathain-Svob census (per the screen; re-verify before relying)
search_order: 1. test the three posted non-symmetric W(25,16) (Dinitz/Munemasa pages; fetch read-only, pin SHA-256) for a symmetric representative in their signed-permutation equivalence class (Goldberger Prop. 5.2 / Valtonen Alg. 3 style), as a cheap low-prior check
2. structured symmetric models: 5x5 arrays of 5x5 circulants with A_ji = A_ij^T (semiregular Z5), Z3 with one fixed point, involutions; orbit-matrix (quotient) feasibility first, then SAT on lifts
3. general SAT/ILP with symmetry breaking only after structured models are exhausted or bounded
stop_rule: If structured models fail, report exactly which models were exhausted (with certificates or exact counts) and which were bounded/UNKNOWN; no nonexistence claim from restricted models.
rules: no commit/push/publication/external contact (read-only HTTP GET of public pages allowed, pinned by SHA-256); no deletion; no /tmp; no paid APIs; no model CLIs; SIGTERM plus bounded wait only; host-clock timestamps; mode-x files; UNKNOWN for timeouts
